note: Track picking (guitar-techniques), step 2: down and up strokes, four notes a string (picking-drill at level beginner), on one string, across all six, then a little faster. It states its moves (tempo 60 to 100): the first step names the tempo as a param, the last section's drill stays 12 above the first, and no step mentions a selector, since the app brings the faster tempo.

exercise.title: Down and up with the pick
exercise.why: The pick passes the string again on its way back up, so playing on the upstroke too gives you two notes for one movement of the hand.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}} and follow the tab: the open G string, one note per beat. The arrows under the tab show each stroke, down then up.
Stay with it until the upstroke is as loud as the downstroke.

Press Play below to start the metronome. Now the drill moves to the next string after every four notes, across all six strings and back.
If you lose the order of the strokes, say "down, up" out loud as you play.

Press Play below to start the metronome, a little faster now, and play the drill across the strings again.
If the strokes get uneven, play only the open G string until they are even again.
